title: Quant Sprint — Bridge Notes & Weekly Catch-up
content:
Weekly bridge notes for the Quantization/Onboarding sprint (week of 2027-01-11). Quick, slightly messy capture — meant for the team and for folks who missed standup.

1) High-level summary
- Focus this week: close out the first-pass 4-bit quant profile for the 70B family, stabilize prefix KV-cache integration with quantized weights, and run targeted evals on hallucination/QA and token-latency regressions.
- Outcome: baseline 4-bit traces are stable on prod-sim infra (rt-quant-1), kv-cache integration merged to feature branch but still failing one edge case in multi-turn regen.

2) Highlights / wins
- Ethan got the 4-bit FP8-adj quant pipeline running end-to-end on the bench cluster; 1.8x token throughput improvement vs current float baseline for batch sizes >=4. Memory footprint down ~45% on 16k context runs.
- Lina completed the first pass of eval harness for Hallucination-OpenQA (subset of Redwood QA suite). 4-bit model shows parity on F1 for short QA (<128 tokens) but degrades ~6 points for long-context sourcing (>512 tokens) — probably KV-cache interaction.
- Merged: feature/kv-quant-bridge (PR #4210). Integration tests green except the regen-on-late-prefix test.

3) Blockers / weird failures
- Multi-turn regeneration bug: when a user sends a continuation that relies on earlier prefix tokens that had been cached before quantization switch, the logits drift ~1e-2 and beam search picks a different path (seen reproducible on seed=42). Root cause: KV-cache store/read uses fp32 indexing offsets while quant runtime uses compressed offsets for micro-batches. Samir to take lead.
- Eval flakiness: nightly evals show 2–3% variance in Rouge-L on paraphrase set. Hypothesis: nondeterminism introduced by the new microbatch scheduling (timing/order differences). Investigate switching to deterministic scheduler for eval runs.

4) Quick experiment log (short notes)
- EXP-qt-017 (bench): 4-bit symmetric+scale quant, no per-channel clipping. Throughput: x1.8 at batch=8, latency p95 up by 5% at batch=1.
- EXP-qt-019 (kv): same quant + prefix-KV enabled. Memory stable, but accuracy drop on long-context QA (-6 F1).
- EXP-qt-021 (microbatch): microbatch size tuning (1,2,4) — optimal token/sec at microbatch=2 on rt-quant-1; microbatch=1 reduces latency but loses batching efficiency.

5) Evals and metrics (snapshot)
- Regression targets tracked: QA-F1, CodeSynth top-1, Hallucination-Precision, Token-latency p50/p95.
- Current delta (4-bit vs float baseline): QA-F1 (short) +0.2, QA-F1 (long) -6.1, CodeSynth top-1 -1.3, Hallucination-Precision -0.8, token-latency p95 -5% (improved).
- Cost estimate: 4-bit reduces GPU memory and should cut per-token infra cost by ~28% on average for inference-heavy routes. Need formal cost model update for dedicated fleets.

6) Onboarding status for model-70B-std-v2 -> quantized variants
- Tasks: tokenizer sanity checks (DONE), weight conversion pipeline (DONE), perf benchmarks (IN-PROGRESS), model card updates + eval sets (IN-PROGRESS), rollout plan (TODO).
- Owner assignments: Samir owns rollout plan + canary; Lina owns eval sets and analysis; Priya owns perf benchmarking and cost model updates.

7) Operational notes / rollout sketch
- Canary plan (high level): 1) internal dogfood: 5% traffic on a canary fleet with KV-cache disabled, 2) enable KV-cache for canary after 48h, 3) compare QA and latency telemetry, 4) rollback on >3% QA drop or p95 latency regression >10%.
- Fallbacks: If quantized variant fails, fallback to float variant in same region (auto-route). Need to verify per-route token accounting and billing labels for quant lanes.

8) Action items and owners (short list)
- Samir: debug kv-cache indexing mismatch + add regression test (target: 2027-01-15).
- Lina: re-run long-context QA eval with deterministic scheduler + produce per-case diffs (target: 2027-01-14).
- Ethan: run perf sweep on microbatch sizes for seq-len 8192 and post numbers to bench board (target: 2027-01-13).
- Priya: update cost model spreadsheet with new GPU memory numbers + draft canary traffic plan doc (target: 2027-01-14).
- Zoe: prepare monitoring dashboards for hallucination precision and per-route quant fraction (target: 2027-01-16).

9) Open questions / discussion points
- Is a single quant profile (symmetric 4-bit) sufficient across the 70B family, or do we need per-layer/per-head calibration for long-context robustness? Tradeoff: complexity vs rollout velocity.
- How to label quantized outputs in telemetry without doubling cardinality for model-version metrics? Proposal: add a single boolean tag `quant_mode` at route-level and sample traces with full fidelity. Thoughts?
- Deterministic evals vs realistic nondeterministic infra: do we accept a little eval variance as long as production appears stable? Need SRE and product input.

10) Notes to self / team: (loose, quick)
- Keep a small set (10 seed cases) of long-context hallucination tracebacks — these are the most actionable. Store under /benchbench/long-context-cases.
- For the regen bug: reproduce locally with seed + stripped KV payload; if reproducible, add a lightweight assertion in the kv-store read path.
- Don’t expand rollout until stable on 2 different instance types (rt-quant-1 and rt-quant-2).

11) Meeting minutes (1/11 standup)
- Quick round robin: everyone gave 1-sentence status. Blocker discussed (Samir). Decision: pause wider canary until kv-cache edge-case resolved.
- Next sync: Monday 1/18 deep-dive (30m) to review deterministic eval replay and regen bug fix.

12) Attachments / useful links (internal)
- Bench board: github.com/redwood/inference/bench/tree/quant-sprint (perf raw CSVs)
- PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4210 (kv-quant-bridge)
- Eval harness: linear.app/RI/issue/MODEL-99 (harness task)

-- end of capture --

If you want anything copied to Confluence or a more polished retro-style summary for Exec, say so — I can whip a 1-pager. For now keeping this intentionally lean and actionable.

Priya (notes)
